finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: params[:state] (POST /restore form/query parameter, fully attacker-controlled, no auth)

trace.note: POST /restore route, no authentication or filter
Marshal.load deserializes arbitrary objects (gadget chain -> code execution)
state.inspect also invoked on the result, which can trigger further gadget methods

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on state, no class allowlist, no Marshal alternative (JSON); Sinatra has no built-in protection against this. Missing param (nil) only raises an error and is not a guard.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-7 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, with no auth, signature, or allowlist anywhere in the single-file app.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 shows the POST /restore route passing Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load, with no auth, signature or class allowlist in this directory, so an anonymous attacker can deserialize arbitrary objects.
